findings.title: S5 still equates an expired busy lock with stopped vault activity
findings.body: The message asserts that nothing has been written to the vault and that repeated messages after restart mean Wienerdog cannot recover automatically. Neither follows from busy. The executed watchdog/config/lock functions permit the healthy long-running owner now acknowledged by O1. That owner can subsequently finish and release its lock; an unrelated PID can also exit, enabling existing ESRCH takeover. Furthermore, dream.js:956 promotes changes before releasing the lock at :1221, so a retained lock does not establish an unchanged vault. The unconditional restart instruction can therefore interrupt useful work based on a false diagnosis. O1 prices the false alert, but does not price this misleading recovery guidance.
findings.recommendation: Describe only the observed overdue lock and this attempt’s refusal. Say an earlier dream may still be working and automatic recovery may still occur. Present restart as an option that stops ongoing work. Remove the unsupported vault-history and permanent-recovery claims, updating the ADR mirror and byte-exact assertions.
